answer: In an agent marketplace, agents such as nebula, relic, and mesa must each lock a separate bond for 30 days before accepting work, with outstanding payments capped below that bond. A verifiable failure to deliver forfeits the bond to the buyer. Creating more identities does not multiply unsecured credit: an attacker running 1,000 aliases must immobilize 1,000 bonds, and each proven default burns real capital rather than merely a disposable name.
